_meta.note: Fantasy layer for Orbit Accord. Each planet maps to a country group key in data/layers.json; AI shares come from there unchanged.
_meta.powers_note: Non-AI powers (0-3) are ILLUSTRATIVE game tokens, set by team judgement from widely reported trade strengths (e.g., the Netherlands as a top food exporter, the Gulf in energy and sovereign capital). They are not measured data and should not be cited.

planets.name: Titanis
planets.title: High Regent of Titanis
planets.flavor: A gas giant that designs nearly every thinking-engine in the system and hosts most of them.

planets.name: Magnor
planets.title: Grand Steward of Magnor
planets.flavor: A heavy world of refineries and magnet forges; most of the system's rare metals pass through it.

planets.name: Kaigen
planets.title: Sovereign of Kaigen
planets.flavor: An island world whose chemists make the films, wafers and resists every chip forge needs.

planets.name: Fabrion
planets.title: Warden of Fabrion
planets.flavor: A small world with the system's finest chip forges. Everyone needs it; few can protect it.

planets.name: Mnemos
planets.title: Sovereign of Mnemos
planets.flavor: The memory world: four in five high-bandwidth memory stacks are grown here.

planets.name: Lithos
planets.title: Steward of Lithos
planets.flavor: A low, flat world that alone builds the light-machines that print the finest chips.

planets.name: Ferrum
planets.title: Chancellor of Ferrum
planets.flavor: A machine-builder's world: grid equipment, precision tools and a large common market.

planets.name: Albion
planets.title: Crown of Albion
planets.flavor: A world of banks, labs and safety testers, with a strong voice and few factories.

planets.name: Solara
planets.title: Emirs of Solara
planets.flavor: Desert worlds rich in energy and capital, buying their way into thinking-engines.

planets.name: Boreal
planets.title: Twin Sovereigns of Boreal
planets.flavor: Twin wide worlds of grain, gas and ore, far from the chip forges.

planets.name: The Ore Belt
planets.title: Council of the Ore Belt
planets.flavor: A belt of mining worlds whose cobalt, nickel and copper feed every forge, though others own many of the mines.

goals.name: Test frontier minds before release
goals.risk: Dangerous capabilities reaching the public before anyone outside the developer has checked them.
goals.route: Coalition members require pre-release access for their safety institutes as a condition of hosting or of buying chip inputs.
goals.consent: Frontier developers; each member's legislature or regulator; safety institutes with capacity to test.
goals.gap: No evidence yet that a developer would accept testing rather than move hosting elsewhere.

goals.name: One alarm for serious incidents
goals.risk: Serious AI incidents seen in one country but not shared, so others repeat the failure.
goals.route: A shared incident definition, with reports sent to every member.
goals.consent: Regulators in each member; operators running systems on members' territory.
goals.gap: Korea, Singapore and Australia already define incidents differently; harmonising them is untested.

goals.name: Guard the model weights
goals.risk: Model weights stolen from a host's data centre and misused.
goals.route: A common security standard for weights trained or stored on members' territory.
goals.consent: Data-centre operators and developers storing weights locally.
goals.gap: Covers only weights stored on members' soil; little frontier training happens there today.

goals.name: Keep essential services running in a crisis
goals.risk: Governments and hospitals losing AI access overnight if a foreign provider withdraws.
goals.route: Locally hosted models under contracts that survive withdrawal.
goals.consent: Model providers; hosting operators; government buyers.
goals.gap: A frozen copy ages; whether providers sign survivable contracts is unknown.

goals.name: Know where the advanced chips are
goals.risk: Advanced chips diverted to uses agreements forbid, with no way to check.
goals.route: Export licences for chips and key inputs carry a location-reporting condition.
goals.consent: Export-control authorities in each member; chip and tool makers.
goals.gap: Location reporting helps verification but is not sufficient alone; enforcement after export is unproven.

goals.name: A lawful off-switch
goals.risk: A dangerous workload running on a member's soil that no one can lawfully stop.
goals.route: Operators can isolate or stop a workload on a lawful order, with notice and review.
goals.consent: Host courts and regulators; operators; tenants.
goals.gap: Works only while computing is hosted locally; the host's leverage shrinks if computing moves away.

eras.name: Age of Code
eras.text: Progress comes mostly from better ideas. Physical chokepoints matter less.

eras.name: Present Age
eras.text: Roughly today's mix, per gszep's model: about 40% of progress needs new physical things.

eras.name: Age of Forges
eras.text: Progress depends on chips, power and robots. Physical chokepoints matter most.
